topic.title: Brain and Biosignal Representation Learning
topic.overview: This topic learns representations of physiological recordings, especially brain activity measured across time, channels, and regions. Models must distinguish meaningful dynamics from variation in subjects, electrode placement, and recording conditions. Recent approaches connect local signal activity with functional relationships and use multiscale tokenization or attention to capture patterns at different spatial and temporal resolutions.
topic.whyItMatters: Transferable representations could reduce labeled-data requirements for decoding tasks. Standardized evaluation is essential because improved results can reflect adaptation choices or dataset differences rather than a better general model.
topic.evolution: The historical examples include direct cardiac-signal classification and EEG analysis in the late 1980s and early 1990s. More recent work emphasizes unsupervised brain representations and large pretrained models. A 2026 benchmark highlights objective conflicts and negative transfer, showing that scale alone does not explain downstream performance.
openQuestions: Which pretraining objectives preserve neural information needed by diverse downstream tasks?
How can evaluation separate physiological generalization from recording-system familiarity?
